We need propose steps: likely disconnections:

1. Amide formation: between C(=O) and an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So break amide bond to give carboxylic acid (or acid chloride) and aniline.

Target has C(=O)N attached to phenyl with NH (aniline). So step 1 retrosynthesis: break amide to give acid fragment: /C=C/C(=O) (the unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid fragment is cinnamic acid derivative attached to phenyl sulfonyl etc. Actually the fragment is /C=C/C(=O) attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Wait structure: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the unsaturated amide attached to phenyl ring (c2). So the acid precursor would be the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to phenyl (c2). So step 1: amide formation.

2. The unsaturated acid could be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (c2-CHO) and malonic acid to give α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl. So break C=C double bond formation: retro-Doebner: break double bond and carbonyl to give aldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus step 2: retro-Doebner: target unsaturated acid to aldehyde (c2-CHO) + malonic acid.

3. The sulfonamide formation: the sulfonyl group attached to an aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). So break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline. Likely sulfonyl chloride + aniline gives sulfonamide. So step 3: sulfonamide formation.

Thus overall three steps: (1) amide coupling, (2) Doebner modification, (3) sulfonamide formation.
